sections.h2: Where is Longmont and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Longmont is a home rule city in northeastern Boulder County that reaches east into western Weld County. The two-county footprint is the first thing a seller should know, because the county that holds your parcel decides which treasurer bills you and which clerk records your deed.

U.S. Highway 287 runs through the center of town as Main Street. It leads north about 16 miles to Loveland and south about 34 miles to downtown Denver. State Highway 119 crosses the city south of downtown, running about 15 miles southwest to Boulder and about 5 miles east to Interstate 25. St. Vrain Creek flows just south of the city center, and Longs Peak, the mountain the city is named after, is visible from town.

sections.h2: How did Longmont grow into the city it is today?
sections.html:
Longmont began in 1871 as the Chicago-Colorado Colony, a planned town laid out on a grid inside one square mile. It was the first planned community in Boulder County. The Colorado Central Railroad reached the town from Boulder in 1877, and the town incorporated in 1885.

Farming carried the local economy for decades. In the 1960s the federal government built the Denver Air Route Traffic Control Center here and IBM opened a campus nearby. The big Longmont Foods turkey plant on south Main Street, which dated to 1950, closed in 2011 after Butterball bought it.

A newer chapter came in the mid-1990s, when the southern edge of the city became home to Prospect New Town, the first New Urbanist project in Colorado. In 2013 the city council voted to build its own gigabit fiber network, NextLight, and to bring it to every home and business over three years. Population doubled in the 1960s and again in the 1970s, from 11,489 in 1960 to 23,209 in 1970 and 42,942 in 1980, so the housing stock spans several eras.

sections.h2: Who are the largest employers in Longmont?
sections.html:
The biggest employer in Longmont is the school district, followed by the city itself. The city's 2020 financial report ranked the top employers this way:

  • St. Vrain Valley Schools: 3,543 employees
  • City of Longmont: 1,625
  • Seagate Technology: 1,430
  • Intrado: 755
  • Longmont United Hospital: 671
  • UC Health Longs Peak Hospital: 540
  • McLane Western: 460
  • Federal Aviation Administration: 422

By industry, manufacturing employed 7,188 people in 2022, professional, scientific and technical services employed 6,533, and retail trade employed 6,066. Two of the country's largest craft brewers, Left Hand and Oskar Blues, brew locally, and the city's proximity to Rocky Mountain National Park supports hotels, restaurants and outdoor businesses. Amgen closed its Longmont campus in 2015, a reminder that employers here have come and gone.

For a seller, this mix means buyers include school and hospital staff, tech and aerospace workers, and commuters headed to Boulder or Denver. It also means a job change in the household is one of the common reasons a Longmont owner needs to sell on a deadline.

sections.h2: What does Longmont's climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Longmont has a cold semi-arid climate. The record high is 106 degrees Fahrenheit, set in July 1973 and again in June 1994, and the record low is minus 38 degrees, set in January 1930.

That range is hard on a roof, a furnace and an air conditioner. A buyer's inspector will look at all three, and a house with an old roof or a failing heating system is where a conventional sale often stalls. If the house has deferred maintenance, ask for the repair estimates first, then compare a repaired listing against a sale as-is.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and transit serve Longmont?
sections.html:
Public schools in Longmont are run by the St. Vrain Valley School District, and the Boulder County campus of Front Range Community College is in the city. A number of private schools also operate here.

  • RTD buses connect Longmont with Denver and Boulder.
  • The FLEX regional bus links Longmont with Berthoud, Loveland and Fort Collins.
  • RTD's plan to extend the B Line commuter rail to Longmont was described in 2024 as possibly finished in the early 2040s.
  • Vance Brand Airport, owned by the city, has no scheduled passenger flights and mostly serves general aviation.
  • The League of American Bicyclists named Longmont a silver-level bicycle-friendly community in 2012.

Most trips still happen by car, with Highway 119 and Main Street as the two main corridors.

sections.h2: What short-term rental rules apply to a Longmont house?
sections.html:
Longmont requires a license, renewed every year, for any short-term rental, meaning a stay of fewer than 30 days in an entire dwelling or in rooms of an owner-occupied home. A sales and use tax license is also required, existing rentals are not exempt, and unlicensed rentals are subject to code enforcement.

Only Longmont residents can apply, and applications go through the city's Accela Citizen Access system or in person at the Development Services Center at 385 Kimbark Street. Questions go to code enforcement at (303) 651-8695.

This matters when you sell. If the house was ever listed on a platform such as Airbnb or VRBO, confirm the license status before you go under contract, because an unlicensed history can complicate a buyer's questions and an investor's underwriting.

sections.h2: How do property tax payments and recording work when you sell in Longmont?
sections.html:
Colorado lets owners pay property tax in two halves or in one full payment, and Boulder County lists its 2026 dates as March 2 and June 15 for the halves and April 30 for the full amount. March 2 appears because the usual February 28 date fell on a weekend that year. The county notes there are no discounts for early payment.

Late interest at Boulder County starts at 1 percent on a first-half payment made in March and climbs to 6 percent by August, with a different schedule for second-half and full payments. After September, contact the treasurer for exact amounts. The Longmont branch of the treasurer's office is at 515 Coffman Street, Suite 113, and the county's page showed it open on Mondays only.

If your parcel is in the Weld County part of the city, you deal with Weld County instead. Weld's recording page explains that Colorado law charges a state documentary fee of 1 cent per $100 on a transfer for more than $500, so a $400,000 sale carries a $40 fee. It also says every deed must show the grantee's mailing address, which is where future tax statements go.

sections.h2: What should a Longmont seller check before taking a cash offer?
sections.html:
Start with a short list of facts about the property, because they decide how quickly a sale can close.

  • Which county holds the parcel, Boulder or Weld, and whether current taxes are paid.
  • Whether the home has ever operated as a short-term rental and, if so, whether a license was held.
  • Who occupies the house and what the lease says.
  • Any open permits, liens or unpaid utility balances.
  • Roof, furnace and cooling condition, since those are the items a buyer will price first.

Our team can look at a Longmont house in almost any condition. If you want to compare a cash sale with listing, tell us the address and the situation, and we will explain how each route would work for that house.

faqs.q: Is Longmont in Boulder County or Weld County?
faqs.a: Both. Most of Longmont is in Boulder County, and the city extends east into western Weld County. Your tax bill and recorded documents come from the county that holds your parcel.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Boulder County?
faqs.a: Boulder County listed March 2 and June 15 as the 2026 half-payment dates and April 30 as the full-payment date. The usual February 28 date moved because it fell on a weekend.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent my Longmont house short term?
faqs.a: Yes. Longmont requires an annual short-term rental license and a sales and use tax license for any rental of fewer than 30 days. Only Longmont residents are eligible to apply.

faqs.q: What is the state documentary fee on a Colorado home sale?
faqs.a: Colorado charges 1 cent per $100 of consideration on a transfer for more than $500, according to Weld County's recording page. Confirm the amount with your closing agent.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Longmont house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Many owners sell as-is, and a cash buyer prices the repairs into the offer. Comparing that against the cost and time of fixing the house first is a sensible step.
